title: Nature Built a Nuclear Reactor 2 Billion Years Ago
hook: Two billion years before humans, Earth built its own nuclear reactor.
body: In 1972, French scientists testing uranium from Gabon, in Africa, noticed something impossible.
Some of it was missing the exact type of uranium used in nuclear power plants.
Someone... or something... had already used it.
The answer was even stranger. Groundwater had seeped into a rich uranium deposit and started a natural chain reaction.
It switched itself on for about half an hour, boiled the water away, cooled down, and started again.
Scientists think it kept doing this, on and off, for hundreds of thousands of years.
cta: And it all started two billion years before humans.
caption: Earth was running nuclear reactors before we existed ☢️

title: This Frog Hides Its Blood to Become Invisible
hook: This frog makes itself invisible by hiding its own blood.
body: It's called the glass frog, and from underneath you can see its heart beating.
But red blood should give it away. So how does it vanish while it sleeps?
In 2022, scientists finally found out.
When it falls asleep, it pulls almost ninety percent of its red blood cells out of circulation and packs them inside its liver.
Its body becomes up to three times more see-through.
And here's the part scientists still can't explain. Packing that much blood together should cause deadly clots... but it doesn't.
cta: Which is why doctors are studying this tiny frog that hides its own blood.
caption: The frog that turns invisible every night 🐸

title: Voyager 1 Is Now One Full Light-Day Away
hook: Right now, a message to this spacecraft takes an entire day.
body: Voyager 1 launched in 1977, with less computing power than a car key fob.
It's now around 25 billion kilometers away, the farthest object humans have ever made.
It's so far that a radio signal, moving at the speed of light, needs about a full day to reach it.
Its transmitter has roughly the power of a fridge light bulb.
By the time that whisper reaches Earth, it's billions of times weaker than a watch battery.
And yet giant dish antennas still catch it... and NASA still talks back.
cta: So if you said hello today, Voyager would only hear it tomorrow.
caption: One light-day from home 🛰️

title: The Most Remote Place on Earth
hook: At this spot, the closest humans are usually in space.
body: It's called Point Nemo, the place in the ocean farthest from any land.
The nearest shore is about 2,700 kilometers away.
But the International Space Station orbits only about 400 kilometers above Earth.
So when it flies overhead, astronauts are the closest people to you.
And it gets creepier. Space agencies use this exact spot as a graveyard for old spacecraft.
Hundreds of satellites and space station parts now lie on the sea floor down there.
cta: Which makes it the loneliest place on Earth... watched from space.
caption: The ocean's spacecraft cemetery 🌊🛰️

title: The Loudest Sound in Recorded History
hook: This sound was so loud it went around the world several times.
body: In August 1883, the volcano Krakatoa in Indonesia exploded.
People heard it nearly 4,800 kilometers away, on an island near Mauritius.
They thought it was distant gunfire.
Sailors 64 kilometers away reported that it ruptured their eardrums.
But the strangest proof came from weather stations around the planet.
Their pressure gauges recorded the shockwave passing by, again and again, as it circled the Earth for days.
cta: The planet itself rang like a bell... for almost a week.
caption: The loudest sound humans ever recorded 🌋🔊

title: This Shrimp's Snap Is Hotter Than the Sun's Surface
hook: This shrimp shoots a bubble almost as hot as the surface of the Sun.
body: The pistol shrimp is only a few centimeters long.
It has one oversized claw that snaps shut incredibly fast.
That snap shoots out a jet of water that creates a collapsing bubble.
For a split second, the bubble reaches thousands of degrees and even gives off a flash of light.
The pop is one of the loudest sounds in the ocean, loud enough to stun fish.
Colonies of these shrimp are so noisy that they can mess with submarine sonar.
cta: All from a bubble almost as hot as the Sun.
caption: Tiny shrimp, sun-hot punch 🦐🔥

title: The Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways
hook: There's a planet where it rains glass... sideways.
body: It's called HD 189733 b, and from far away it looks like a beautiful blue marble.
But that blue doesn't come from water.
Scientists think it comes from tiny particles of silicate, basically glass, in its atmosphere.
Its winds may reach around 8,700 kilometers per hour, about seven times the speed of sound.
So that glass doesn't fall down. It gets blasted sideways.
And its daytime temperature is more than 900 degrees Celsius.
cta: The prettiest blue planet... is the one place you'd never want to visit.
caption: Blue, beautiful and deadly 🪐

title: There's a Giant Alcohol Cloud in Space
hook: There's a cloud in space filled with alcohol, and it might smell like raspberries.
body: Near the center of our galaxy is a huge gas cloud called Sagittarius B2.
Astronomers found it contains enormous amounts of alcohol molecules.
Then, in 2009, they found a chemical called ethyl formate in it.
On Earth, that chemical helps give raspberries their flavor, and it smells a bit like rum.
Before you plan a trip... the cloud also contains toxic chemicals, and it's 26,000 light-years away.
cta: So the center of our galaxy might smell like raspberries and rum.
caption: The galaxy's strangest bar 🍓🌌

title: The Lake That Turns Animals Into Statues
hook: This lake can turn dead animals into stone-like statues.
body: Lake Natron in Tanzania looks blood red from above.
Its water is extremely salty and alkaline, sometimes almost as harsh as ammonia.
When birds die there, the minerals preserve their bodies, hardening them almost like statues.
A photographer found these calcified birds along the shore and posed them for haunting photos.
But here's the twist. The same deadly lake is the main breeding ground for millions of flamingos.
Its harsh water keeps predators away from their nests.
cta: A lake that preserves the dead... and protects the living.
caption: Nature's most deadly nursery 🦩

title: The Boiling River of the Amazon
hook: Deep in the Amazon, there's a river that can cook animals alive.
body: For years, scientists thought it was just a legend.
Then geoscientist Andrés Ruzo went looking for it in Peru.
He found a river about six kilometers long, with stretches that reach close to 100 degrees Celsius.
Small animals that fall in can be cooked in seconds.
The strangest part? There's no active volcano nearby.
Scientists believe rainwater sinks deep underground, gets heated by the Earth, and comes back up through cracks.
cta: Proof that some legends... are real.
caption: The Amazon's boiling secret 🔥🌊

title: The Wow! Signal Was Never Explained
hook: In 1977, a telescope picked up a signal so strange, an astronomer wrote 'Wow!' next to it.
body: The Big Ear radio telescope in Ohio was scanning the sky for signs of alien life.
Suddenly, a powerful signal appeared, lasting about 72 seconds.
It was on a frequency that's naturally quiet, a frequency scientists had predicted aliens might use.
Astronomer Jerry Ehman circled it on the printout and wrote one word... Wow.
Scientists have pointed telescopes at that patch of sky many times since.
It has never been heard again.
cta: And nobody knows for sure what said 'wow' back.
caption: Still unexplained 👽📡

title: The War Australia Lost to Birds
hook: Australia once declared war on birds... and lost.
body: In 1932, around 20,000 emus invaded farmland in Western Australia, destroying crops.
So the government sent soldiers armed with machine guns.
But the emus split into small groups and ran in every direction.
They could take bullets and keep running at up to 50 kilometers per hour.
After weeks of trying, the military pulled out.
The commander even said that if he had an army that could take bullets like these birds, he could face any army in the world.
cta: The emus won.
caption: History's most embarrassing war 🐦⚔️

title: The Dancing Plague of 1518
hook: In 1518, hundreds of people couldn't stop dancing.
body: It started in Strasbourg, when a woman stepped into the street and began dancing.
She danced for days.
Within weeks, hundreds of people had joined her, unable to stop.
Officials thought the cure was more dancing, so they built a stage and hired musicians.
It made everything worse.
Historians still debate what caused it. The most popular theory is mass stress during a time of famine and disease.
cta: To this day, no one can fully explain why they couldn't stop.
caption: The strangest epidemic in history 💃

title: The Solar Storm That Set Telegraphs on Fire
hook: In 1859, the Sun set telegraph machines on fire.
body: On September 1st, astronomer Richard Carrington saw a blinding flash on the Sun.
Hours later, the biggest solar storm ever recorded slammed into Earth.
Auroras lit up the sky as far south as the Caribbean.
Some people woke up and started making breakfast, thinking it was morning.
Telegraph operators got electric shocks, and some machines threw sparks.
Some kept working even with their batteries disconnected, powered by the storm itself.
cta: Scientists warn that a storm that big today could knock out power grids around the world.
caption: When the Sun attacked Earth ☀️⚡

title: The Fish That Fights With Slime
hook: This fish can turn a cup of water into a bucket of slime in under a second.
body: Meet the hagfish. It has no jaw, no real spine, and it's been around for hundreds of millions of years.
When a shark bites it, the hagfish releases a tiny amount of slime.
That slime expands in seawater, thousands of times its size, almost instantly.
It clogs the shark's gills, and the shark spits it out, gagging.
To clean itself, the hagfish ties its own body into a knot and slides it down to scrape the slime off.
cta: Ugly? Maybe. But it's survived longer than the dinosaurs.
caption: The ocean's slime master 🐟

title: This Moon Shoots Oceans Into Space
hook: There's a moon that sprays its ocean into space.
body: It's called Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons, and it's covered in ice.
In 2005, NASA's Cassini spacecraft spotted giant jets shooting from its south pole.
They're water, blasting out from a hidden ocean under the ice.
Cassini later flew straight through these plumes and tasted them.
It found salt, organic molecules, and signs of hydrothermal activity, like vents on Earth's seafloor.
On Earth, places like that are packed with life.
cta: Which makes this tiny moon one of the best places to look for aliens.
caption: An ocean hiding under the ice 🌊🪐

title: The Loneliest Whale in the World
hook: Somewhere in the Pacific, a whale has been calling for decades... and nobody answers.
body: In 1989, the US Navy began tracking a strange whale song.
Most large whales call at very low frequencies.
But this whale sings at about 52 hertz, much higher than the others.
Scientists believe other whales may not recognize its voice.
It's been tracked year after year, wandering alone across the ocean.
No one has ever confirmed seeing it.
cta: The world calls it the loneliest whale... still singing out there right now.
caption: Still singing, still alone 🐋

title: Your Brain Can't Feel Pain
hook: Surgeons can operate on your brain while you're awake.
body: It sounds terrifying, but it happens in hospitals around the world.
Your brain processes all the pain you feel.
But the brain tissue itself has no pain receptors.
So after numbing the scalp and skull, doctors can wake patients up during surgery.
Some patients talk, play instruments, or answer questions while surgeons work.
That helps doctors make sure they don't damage areas that control speech or movement.
cta: The organ that feels everything... can't feel itself.
caption: Wide awake brain surgery 🧠

title: Your Body Glows in the Dark
hook: Your body is glowing right now. You just can't see it.
body: In 2009, Japanese scientists filmed people with ultra-sensitive cameras in total darkness.
The cameras caught a faint glow coming from their bodies.
It's about a thousand times too weak for human eyes to see.
The light comes from chemical reactions in our cells.
And it changes through the day. It was brightest in the late afternoon and dimmest late at night.
The face glowed the most.
cta: So technically... you glow.
caption: Humans literally glow ✨

title: The Sahara Used to Be Green
hook: The Sahara Desert was once full of lakes, hippos, and crocodiles.
body: Between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago, North Africa was much wetter.
Scientists call it the African Humid Period.
Grasslands covered much of the Sahara, and giant lakes filled its basins.
Ancient rock art there shows swimmers, cattle, and giraffes.
Then small wobbles in Earth's orbit shifted the monsoon rains away.
And over a few thousand years, the green land turned into the desert we know.
cta: And scientists think one day... it could turn green again.
caption: When the Sahara was green 🌿🏜️

title: A Man Knocked Down a Wall and Found a City
hook: A man knocked down a wall in his house... and found an entire underground city.
body: It happened in 1963, in Cappadocia, Turkey.
Behind the wall was a tunnel. And the tunnel led down.
Explorers discovered a city carved deep into the rock, many levels underground.
It had stables, chapels, kitchens, wells, and air shafts.
Experts estimate it could shelter thousands of people, along with their animals.
Huge rolling stone doors could seal it from the inside during attacks.
cta: And it all started with one wall.
caption: The city under the house 🏛️

title: What Divers Found at the Bottom of the Ocean
hook: At the deepest point on Earth, scientists found... a plastic bag.
body: The Mariana Trench plunges nearly 11 kilometers below the surface.
If you dropped Mount Everest inside, its peak would still be underwater.
The pressure there is over a thousand times what you feel at sea level.
Very few humans have ever been down there.
But when scientists reviewed deep sea footage, they found a plastic bag at almost eleven kilometers deep.
Researchers have also found tiny bits of plastic inside creatures living in the trench.
cta: We reached the deepest place on Earth... and our trash got there first.
caption: Our trash got there first 🌊

title: The Strongest Material in the Universe Is Called Pasta
hook: The strongest material in the universe is called nuclear pasta.
body: It forms deep in the crust of neutron stars, the collapsed cores of giant stars.
The pressure there is so extreme that atomic nuclei get squeezed into strange shapes.
Flat sheets, like lasagna. Long strands, like spaghetti.
That's how it got its name.
Computer simulations suggest it could be about ten billion times stronger than steel.
cta: So the toughest thing in the universe... is shaped like dinner.
caption: Lasagna, but cosmic 🍝🌌

title: The Man Who Hiccupped for 68 Years
hook: One man hiccupped every day... for sixty-eight years.
body: In 1922, Charles Osborne, a farmer from Iowa, was lifting a heavy hog.
He fell and started hiccupping.
Then he just... never stopped.
At first, he hiccupped around forty times a minute.
He still married, raised children, and lived a mostly normal life.
Then, in 1990, the hiccups suddenly stopped on their own. He died about a year later.
cta: Doctors never found a cure.
caption: Sixty-eight years of hiccups 😮

title: Her Cells Are Still Alive Today
hook: A woman who died in 1951 still has living cells in labs today.
body: Her name was Henrietta Lacks.
While she was being treated for cancer, doctors took a sample of her cells without asking her.
Most human cells die after dividing a limited number of times.
But hers kept dividing, again and again.
They became known as HeLa cells, and they helped develop the polio vaccine and countless medical discoveries.
Her family didn't learn about it for decades.
cta: Her cells changed medicine forever... and she never knew.
caption: The woman whose cells never died 🧬

title: The Animal That Survived Outer Space
hook: This animal survived being thrown into outer space.
body: It's called a tardigrade, or water bear, and it's smaller than a grain of sand.
When things get rough, it dries itself out and curls into a ball called a tun.
In 2007, scientists strapped tardigrades to a satellite and exposed them to space.
Back on Earth, some of them woke up, and some even had babies.
They can survive freezing, boiling, and extreme radiation.
cta: If anything outlives us on this planet... it might be this.
caption: The toughest animal alive 🐻

title: The Deepest Hole Ever Dug
hook: Humans dug the deepest hole in history... and barely scratched the Earth.
body: In 1970, Soviet scientists started drilling a hole in northern Russia.
They kept going for nearly twenty years.
They reached about 12 kilometers deep, deeper than the ocean's deepest point.
Down there, rocks were around 180 degrees Celsius, and they found microscopic fossils.
But the heat made the rock behave almost like plastic, and the drill couldn't continue.
And that 12 kilometers? It's only about a third of the way through the continental crust.
cta: Today it's just sealed with a small metal cap.
caption: The deepest hole ever dug 🕳️

title: The Bloop: The Ocean's Mystery Sound
hook: In 1997, underwater microphones caught a sound louder than any known animal.
body: Scientists named it The Bloop.
It was picked up by sensors thousands of kilometers apart in the Pacific Ocean.
Some people believed it came from a giant sea creature no one had ever seen.
It became one of the internet's favorite mysteries.
Years later, scientists found the most likely answer.
Huge icebergs cracking and breaking apart near Antarctica make sounds just like it.
cta: Not a monster... but the sound of ice tearing itself apart.
caption: The ocean's mystery sound 🔊🌊

title: Scientists Warned Against Creating Mirror Life
hook: In 2024, top scientists warned the world not to build one type of life.
body: Almost all life on Earth is built from molecules that twist in one direction.
Like a left hand.
So scientists asked... what if we built bacteria from mirror image molecules?
Over thirty researchers studied the idea, and many came away alarmed.
Our immune systems might not even recognize mirror bacteria, so they could spread without being stopped.
So they asked labs around the world not to create it.
cta: Some ideas are too dangerous to try.
caption: The life we shouldn't create 🧬⚠️

title: Lightning Can Turn Sand Into Glass
hook: When lightning strikes sand, it leaves behind tubes of glass.
body: A lightning bolt can be several times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
When it hits sand or dry soil, it melts the grains instantly.
The molten sand cools and hardens into hollow, branching glass tubes.
They're called fulgurites, which means lightning rocks.
Some trace the exact path the lightning took into the ground, like a frozen bolt.
cta: Basically... a lightning bolt, frozen in glass.
caption: Lightning, frozen in glass ⚡

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts
hook: This animal has three hearts and blue blood.
body: The octopus has two hearts that pump blood to its gills, and one that pumps it to the rest of its body.
Its blood is blue because it uses copper, not iron, to carry oxygen.
Here's the wild part. The main heart actually stops beating when the octopus swims.
That's why octopuses prefer crawling. Swimming exhausts them.
cta: Follow for a new mind-blowing fact every day.
caption: Three hearts, blue blood, and it hates swimming 🐙

title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than a Year
hook: On Venus, a single day lasts longer than a year.
body: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin around once.
But it only needs about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.
So one day on Venus is longer than its entire year.
And it spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
cta: Follow for more facts that sound fake but aren't.
caption: Your birthday would come before tomorrow on Venus 🪐

title: Bananas Are Berries. Strawberries Aren't.
hook: Botanically, a banana is a berry. A strawberry is not.
body: To a botanist, a berry is a fruit that grows from one flower with one ovary.
Bananas, grapes, tomatoes, and even avocados fit that definition.
Strawberries don't, because those tiny seeds on the outside are actually separate fruits.
So the fruit named berry isn't one, and the banana secretly is.
cta: Comment the fruit fact that surprised you most.
caption: Botany is chaos 🍌🍓

title: Babies Have More Bones Than You
hook: You were born with almost 100 more bones than you have now.
body: Newborn babies have around 300 bones and pieces of cartilage.
As they grow, many of these bones slowly fuse together.
The skull alone starts as several separate plates so the head can fit through birth.
By adulthood, most people end up with 206 bones.
cta: Follow for a new fact about your body every day.
caption: Where did the other 94 bones go? 🦴

title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
hook: Sharks were swimming in the ocean before trees existed.
body: The earliest sharks appeared around 450 million years ago.
The first true trees showed up around 385 million years ago.
That means sharks are older than trees by tens of millions of years.
They've survived five mass extinctions, including the one that wiped out the dinosaurs.
cta: Follow if this blew your mind.
caption: Sharks: older than trees, survived 5 mass extinctions 🦈

title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the Moon Landing Than the Pyramids
hook: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the pyramids.
body: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 2560 BC.
Cleopatra ruled Egypt around 50 BC, about 2500 years later.
The Moon landing happened in 1969, about 2000 years after Cleopatra.
To her, the pyramids were already ancient history.
cta: Follow for history facts that break your brain.
caption: Time is weird 🏛️🚀

title: A Spoon of Neutron Star Weighs a Billion Tons
hook: A single teaspoon of this star would weigh about a billion tons.
body: A neutron star is what's left after a giant star collapses.
It packs more mass than our Sun into a ball about 20 kilometers wide.
It's so dense that one teaspoon of it would weigh around a billion tons on Earth.
Some of them spin hundreds of times every second.
cta: Follow for a new space fact every day.
caption: The densest objects in the universe 🌌

title: Wombats Poop Cubes
hook: There's an animal on Earth that poops perfect cubes.
body: It's the wombat, a small burrowing marsupial from Australia.
Scientists found the cubes form inside its intestines, thanks to stretchy and stiff sections of the gut wall.
Wombats leave up to a hundred cubes a night to mark their territory.
The flat sides help stop them rolling away.
cta: Share this with someone who needs a weird fact today.
caption: Nature really said ⬛ 💩

title: Your Stomach Rebuilds Itself Every Few Days
hook: Your stomach would digest itself if it didn't do this.
body: Your stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve some metals.
To survive, the stomach coats itself in a thick layer of protective mucus.
The cells of its inner lining are also replaced every few days.
So you're constantly growing a brand new stomach lining.
cta: Follow for more facts about your own body.
caption: Your body is doing a lot right now 🧬

title: Oxford University Is Older Than the Aztec Empire
hook: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
body: Teaching at Oxford was already happening by 1096.
The Aztec capital, Tenochtitlan, wasn't founded until 1325.
That's more than 200 years later.
Students were studying at Oxford before the Aztec Empire even began.
cta: Follow for history facts you never learned in school.
caption: History timelines are wild 📚

title: More Trees on Earth Than Stars in Our Galaxy
hook: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
body: A major study estimated Earth has about three trillion trees.
Our galaxy has roughly 100 to 400 billion stars.
So trees win by a huge margin.
Sadly, scientists say we've lost almost half of all trees since humans started farming.
cta: Comment if you'd plant a tree today.
caption: Earth's forests are bigger than you think 🌲✨

title: Lightning Is Hotter Than the Sun
hook: A lightning bolt is about five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
body: A lightning strike can heat the air to around 30,000 degrees Celsius.
The surface of the Sun is about 5,500 degrees Celsius.
That sudden heat makes the air explode outward.
That explosion is the sound you hear as thunder.
cta: Follow for science facts every day.
caption: Thunder is literally exploding air ⚡

title: Sea Otters Hold Hands While Sleeping
hook: Sea otters hold hands so they don't lose each other.
body: Sea otters often sleep floating on their backs in the water.
To avoid drifting apart, they sometimes hold paws or wrap themselves in kelp.
A floating group of otters is called a raft.
Some rafts have been seen with more than a thousand otters.
cta: Send this to someone you'd hold hands with.
caption: The cutest survival strategy 🦦

title: Moon Footprints Could Last Millions of Years
hook: The footprints on the Moon could last for millions of years.
body: The Moon has no wind and no rain to wipe them away.
So the boot prints left by Apollo astronauts are still there today.
Only tiny meteorite impacts slowly disturb the dust.
Scientists think they could stay visible for millions of years.
cta: Follow for space facts every single day.
caption: Footprints that may outlast humanity 🌕👣

title: Your DNA Could Reach Pluto and Back
hook: The DNA in your body could stretch to Pluto and back.
body: Each of your cells holds about two meters of DNA, tightly coiled.
You have tens of trillions of cells.
Uncoiled and laid end to end, all that DNA would be billions of kilometers long.
That's enough to reach Pluto and come back, several times.
cta: Follow for facts that change how you see yourself.
caption: You are bigger on the inside 🧬

title: Cows Have Best Friends
hook: Cows have best friends, and they get stressed without them.
body: Researchers measured cows' heart rates and stress levels in different pairings.
Cows paired with a preferred companion were noticeably calmer.
When separated from that friend, their stress went up.
Cows are social animals that form real bonds.
cta: Tag your best friend.
caption: Even cows have a bestie 🐄❤️

title: The Eiffel Tower Grows in Summer
hook: The Eiffel Tower gets taller every summer.
body: The tower is made of iron, which expands when it heats up.
On hot summer days, it can grow by up to about 15 centimeters.
When it cools down in winter, it shrinks back.
Its top can even lean slightly away from the Sun as one side heats up.
cta: Follow for facts about the world's famous places.
caption: A tower that breathes with the seasons 🗼

title: Saturn Would Float in Water
hook: Saturn would float in a big enough bathtub.
body: Saturn is the second biggest planet in our solar system.
But it's made mostly of hydrogen and helium gas.
Its average density is lower than water.
So if you could find a bathtub big enough, Saturn would float.
cta: Follow for more space facts.
caption: The planet that could float 🪐🛁

title: The Largest Desert Isn't the Sahara
hook: The world's biggest desert is covered in ice.
body: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow it gets, not by heat.
Antarctica gets so little precipitation that it counts as a desert.
At about 14 million square kilometers, it's the largest desert on Earth.
Some valleys there haven't seen rain in a very, very long time.
cta: Comment if you guessed the Sahara.
caption: Deserts don't have to be hot ❄️

title: Scotland's National Animal Is a Unicorn
hook: Scotland's official national animal is a unicorn.
body: The unicorn has been a symbol of Scotland since the 1300s.
In Celtic legend it stood for purity, power, and independence.
It was believed to be untameable, just like the Scots saw themselves.
You can still see unicorns on the royal coat of arms today.
cta: Follow for history facts that sound made up.
caption: Of course it's a unicorn 🦄🏴

title: A Hummingbird's Heart Beats 1,200 Times a Minute
hook: This bird's heart can beat over 1,200 times a minute.
body: Hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of almost any animal.
Their wings can beat around 50 times every second.
To keep up, they eat nectar from hundreds of flowers a day.
At night they can drop into a deep sleep called torpor to save energy.
cta: Follow for a new animal fact every day.
caption: Tiny bird, huge engine 🐦

title: Your Brain Is an Energy Monster
hook: Your brain is two percent of your weight but eats twenty percent of your energy.
body: The average brain weighs around 1.4 kilograms.
Yet it uses about a fifth of all the energy your body burns at rest.
It has roughly 86 billion neurons sending signals all day long.
Even while you sleep, it never really switches off.
cta: Follow for facts about your amazing body.
caption: Thinking is expensive 🧠

title: The Mantis Shrimp Punches Like a Bullet
hook: This tiny shrimp can punch hard enough to break glass.
body: The mantis shrimp strikes with its club at incredible speed.
The punch is so fast it boils the water around it for an instant.
That creates a second shockwave that hits its prey again.
Some have cracked the glass of their aquarium tanks.
cta: Follow for the craziest animals on Earth.
caption: The ocean's heavyweight champion 🦐🥊

title: Your Water May Be Older Than the Sun
hook: The water you drink may be older than the Sun.
body: Scientists studied the chemistry of water across our solar system.
They found that a large share of it likely formed in interstellar space.
That's before our Sun was even born, over 4.6 billion years ago.
So some of the water in your glass is literally ancient space ice.
cta: Follow for facts that change how you see the world.
caption: Drinking ancient space water 💧🌌

title: The Shortest War Lasted Under an Hour
hook: The shortest war in history lasted less than an hour.
body: In 1896, Britain and Zanzibar went to war.
British ships opened fire on the sultan's palace.
Somewhere between 38 and 45 minutes later, it was over.
It's known as the Anglo-Zanzibar War, the shortest recorded war in history.
cta: Follow for history facts you'll want to repeat.
caption: Blink and you missed it ⏱️

title: Bamboo Can Grow a Meter in a Day
hook: Some bamboo can grow almost a meter in a single day.
body: Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth.
Certain species can grow up to about 90 centimeters in 24 hours.
On a quiet day, you can almost watch it get taller.
Even though it looks like a tree, bamboo is actually a giant grass.

title: The Tallest Mountain Is on Mars
hook: The tallest volcano in the solar system is two and a half times taller than Everest.
body: It's called Olympus Mons, and it's on Mars.
It rises about 22 kilometers above its surroundings.
Mount Everest is less than 9 kilometers tall.
Its base is so wide it would almost cover the state of Arizona.
cta: Follow for space facts every day.
caption: Everest is tiny compared to this 🔴🌋

title: Butterflies Taste With Their Feet
hook: Butterflies taste their food with their feet.
body: Butterflies have taste sensors on their feet.
When they land on a leaf, they can tell instantly if it's the right plant.
Females use this to find the perfect leaf to lay their eggs on.
So every landing is basically a quick taste test.
cta: Share this with someone who loves nature.
caption: Taste testing with every step 🦋

title: You Can't See the Great Wall From Space
hook: One of the most famous facts in the world is false.
body: Many people believe you can see the Great Wall of China from space.
But astronauts say it's nearly impossible to spot with the naked eye.
The wall is very long but only a few meters wide, and it blends into the land.
Big cities at night are far easier to see from orbit.
cta: Follow for facts that bust popular myths.
caption: Myth: busted 🧱🚀

title: Elephants Recognize Themselves in Mirrors
hook: Elephants can recognize themselves in a mirror.
body: Scientists painted a mark on elephants' heads that they could only see in a mirror.
Some elephants touched the mark with their trunk while looking at their reflection.
That means they understood the reflection was themselves.
Only a few animals pass this test, like great apes and dolphins.
cta: Follow for the smartest animals on Earth.
caption: Self-aware giants 🐘🪞

title: Space Is Completely Silent
hook: If you screamed in space, no one would hear you.
body: Sound needs something to travel through, like air or water.
Space is almost a perfect vacuum, so sound waves have nothing to move through.
Even huge explosions in space make no sound at all.
Astronauts talk using radios, which use light-speed radio waves instead.
